data.name: ERROR_TYHP4157
data.value: Typed property `${0}` is possibly uninitialized here; declare `?T ${0} = null`, add an initializer, or guard the read with `??` / `isset`
data.comment: Checker: typed instance property may be unreadably uninitialized (Prop-init #7)

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4157
data.value:
PHP throws "Typed property must not be accessed before initialization" when a typed property has no initializer, is not set by constructor property promotion, and has not been definitely assigned on every constructor path before it is read.
Prefer declaring the property as nullable with an explicit null default (`?T $prop = null`) when the code does not need to distinguish "no value" from "value is null". Otherwise assign it in the constructor on all paths, or guard the read with `??` / `isset` (which do not throw on uninitialized typed properties).
Assignment via a helper method called from the constructor does not count — only a direct `$this->prop = …` in the constructor body (or a declaration-level initializer / promoted parameter) is a guaranteed source.

data.name: ERROR_TYHP4158
data.value: Cannot `unset` typed property `${0}` without `#[\Tyhp\AllowUnset]`; prefer `?T ${0} = null`, or add the attribute when distinguishing uninitialized from null is required
data.comment: Checker: unset of typed property without AllowUnset (Prop-init #8)

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4158
data.value:
PHP's unset() on a typed property returns the slot to the uninitialized state, which defeats property-initialization analysis.
Prefer declaring the property as nullable with an explicit null default (`?T $prop = null`) when "no value" and null are the same. Only opt in with `#[\Tyhp\AllowUnset]` when code genuinely needs the uninitialized state; then every unguarded read may report TYHP4157, and unset itself clears definite-initialization within the method.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4160
data.value:
`mixed` is Tyhp's strict top type: any value may be assigned to it, but it cannot be used in type-specific operations until narrowed.
Narrow with a type guard (`instanceof` / `is`, `\is_string()`, `\is_int()`, a user-defined `$param is T` guard, or a null check) before member access, calls, indexing, arithmetic, bitwise ops, string concatenation, or similar. Comparison and `instanceof`/`is` themselves are allowed so narrowing remains possible.
Assignment and return already reject passing `mixed` where a more specific type is required (TYHP4008 / TYHP4009 / TYHP4010).

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4162
data.value:
The pipe operator (`|>`) passes the left-hand value as the sole argument to the right-hand callable. The RHS must be a Closure, first-class callable, `callable`/`\Closure`-typed value, or an object with `__invoke`.
Replace the RHS with a single-argument callable (for example `strlen(...)` or `(fn($x) => …)`).

data.comment: Checker PHP 8.5 pipe operator RHS has wrong arity

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4163
data.value:
The pipe operator (`|>`) has invalid arity: PHP pipes the left-hand value as a single argument. Callables with more than one required parameter, or with zero parameters, cannot be used on the RHS.
Wrap multi-argument callees in a Closure or arrow function that supplies the extra arguments, e.g. `(fn($x) => \str_replace('a', 'b', $x))`.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4164
data.value:
Piped values are temporaries, so callables whose first parameter is by-reference are rejected (for example `\array_pop(...)`).
Wrap the call in a Closure that takes the value by value and forwards a local variable by reference if mutation is required.

data.name: WARNING_TYHP4165
data.value: Return value of `{0}` is marked `#[\NoDiscard]` and must be used or discarded with `(void)`{1}
data.comment: Checker PHP 8.5 NoDiscard return discarded without (void). {1} is empty, or ": {message}" when #[\NoDiscard] $message is a string literal.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4165
data.value:
`#[\NoDiscard]` marks a function or method whose return value should be used. An unused return is TYHP4165. When `$message` is a string literal, that text is appended to the warning after a colon.
Use the return value (assignment, argument, condition, and so on), or cast with `(void)` to mark an intentional discard: `(void)important();`. Assignment to `$_` also counts as a use.
The warning comes from the invoked declaration. Calling through an interface or abstract method does not warn, even if that declaration is marked. An override does not inherit the warning unless it is itself marked. A trait-imported method keeps the attribute.
Tyhp reports this even when `output.phpVersion` is below 8.5 (PHP's runtime warning is a no-op on older minors). The `(void)` cast is native on 8.5 or later and is omitted from emitted PHP below 8.5.

data.name: ERROR_TYHP4166

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4166
data.value:
PHP 8.4 rejects overriding a `final` property hook at class-declaration time, the same as overriding a final method. `final get` and `final set` are independent — only the hook marked `final` is sealed.
Remove the overriding hook from the child, or drop `final` from the ancestor hook if the override is intentional.

data.name: ERROR_TYHP4167
data.value: By-ref property hook `&get` requires PHP `8.4` or later; target is `{0}`
data.comment: Checker: &get cannot be polyfilled for PHP < 8.4 (silent by-value lowering would lose aliasing)

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4167
data.value:
PHP 8.4 native property hooks support `&get` so `$ref = &$obj->prop` (and array-element writes that rely on by-ref get) can alias backing storage.
When `output.phpVersion` is below 8.4, Tyhp lowers hooks through magic `__get`, which cannot return by reference. Emitting an ordinary by-value get would silently change program semantics, so Tyhp reports an error instead.
Raise `output.phpVersion` to `8.4` or later to keep native `&get`, or rewrite the property to a by-value `get` hook if by-ref aliasing is not required.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4174
data.value: A spliced extension member substitutes the caller's argument where the parameter stood. A parameter the expression writes (assignment, compound assignment, `++` / `--` in either position, or passing to a callee's `&` parameter) must be declared `&`, and only those parameters may be. Write a non-mutating increment as `$v + 1`. Writing `$this` without the `&$this` receiver annotation is `TYHP4369`; annotating `&$this` on a member that never writes `$this` is `TYHP4370`.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4179
data.value: A spliced expression is evaluated at the call site, not inside the declaring class. The body may only reference members at least as accessible as the spliced member itself: a public member's body may reference public members only; a protected body may reference protected and public; a private body may reference any member of the declaring class.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4180
data.value: A `&` parameter requires an argument PHP can bind as a reference. The receiver of a member annotated `&$this` is that argument. Literals, constants, call results, `readonly` properties, and properties whose read path is by value (`{ get; }` in tyhpdef, `__get`, or `offsetGet`) are not referenceable. A tyhpdef `{ &get; }` is. Pass a variable, a non-readonly stored property, or a `{ &get; }` / `&__get` / `&offsetGet` path instead.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4181
data.value: A short `=>` Tyhp extension member and a tyhpdef thin mapping have no PHP method. If the call site cannot be spliced without dropping an argument, delaying it, reordering side effects, or needing a reference-bound local with no statement slot, the compiler reports this error. Bind the argument to a variable first, or (on a Tyhp `extension { }` member) switch to a single-`return` brace body so a PHP method exists to call.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4182
data.value: A function call whose name does not resolve to any declared function, tyhpdef stub, `use function` import, or compile-time builtin is undefined. The binder does not bind call-site function names; the checker resolves them from the enclosing namespace, imports, and the global table. A PHP-version gate (`declare(php=…)` / `#[\Tyhp\Php]`) that is inactive for `output.phpVersion` omits the symbol, so a call outside that gate is the same error. Declare the function, import it, raise the compile target, or fix the name.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP5019
data.value:
Overloaded `++` / `--` rewrites to a method call plus write-back. Postfix forms must yield the value from before that write-back, which the emitter does by splitting into preceding statements (`$__old = $a; $a = Type::__increment($a);` … `$__old`).
That split is not safe inside short-circuit operands (`&&`, `||`, `??`), ternary arms, `else if` conditions (reached only when earlier conditions in the chain were false), or loop conditions that re-evaluate each iteration. Move the postfix into its own statement (or use prefix `++$a` when the new value is intended), then use the captured variable in the expression.

data.value:
A catch-all for parser/lexer errors that do not match a more specific code. The `{0}` placeholder contains the underlying error message from the ANTLR4 parser.
```tyhp <?tyhp // Invalid token that confuses the lexer class #invalid { } ```

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP1003
data.value:
The parser encountered too many errors and aborted processing for the current file. Earlier errors in the same file typically cause this.
Fix: Fix the earlier parser errors in the same file and recompile. Once the foundational syntax issues are resolved, this error will no longer appear.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP1003 (tyhp --explain); recovered from pre-generated diagnostics_reference.md

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP2001
data.value:
A catch-all for unexpected errors during AST generation. This typically indicates an internal compiler issue.
Fix: If you encounter this error, simplify the code near the indicated location and try again. If the error persists, please report it as a compiler bug.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP2002
data.value:
The visitor hit an unexpected grammar alternative while walking the parse tree (a production the AST builder does not handle). This may occur with unusual or edge-case syntax combinations.
Fix: Simplify the expression or statement. If the syntax is valid PHP/Tyhp, this may indicate a compiler limitation -- please report it.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP2002 (tyhp --explain); recovered from pre-generated diagnostics_reference.md

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP2003
data.value:
A required component of a language construct was not found in the parse tree. This often results from incomplete or malformed syntax.
```tyhp <?tyhp // Missing class body class User ```
Fix: Ensure the construct is syntactically complete. Classes need bodies (`{ }`), functions need parameter lists and bodies, etc.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP2003 (tyhp --explain); recovered from pre-generated diagnostics_reference.md

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP2004
data.value:
The code uses a PHP language construct that the Tyhp compiler does not yet support.
Fix: Use an alternative approach that is supported by the compiler. Check the Tyhp documentation for supported constructs and any known limitations.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP2004 (tyhp --explain); recovered from pre-generated diagnostics_reference.md

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP3001
data.value:
A catch-all for unexpected errors during the binding phase.
Fix: If you encounter this error, please report it as a compiler bug with a minimal reproduction.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP3001 (tyhp --explain); recovered from pre-generated diagnostics_reference.md

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP3002
data.value:
Two declarations with the same name exist in the same scope. This includes classes, functions, constants, and variables declared at the same scope level.
The primary span is the later declaration. A secondary span labeled "declared here" points at the first declaration of that name.
```tyhp <?tyhp class User { } // first declaration — labeled "declared here" class User { } // Error: Duplicate declaration of symbol `User` ```
Fix: Rename one of the duplicate declarations, or remove the duplicate. If the declarations are in different files, ensure they are in different namespaces.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP3002 (tyhp --explain); recovered from pre-generated diagnostics_reference.md

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP3003
data.value:
A referenced class, function, constant, variable, or other symbol could not be resolved in any accessible scope. Type names on `is` / `instanceof` / `typeof`, and undeclared names inside generic type arguments, use this same diagnostic.
```tyhp <?tyhp function demo(mixed $x): bool { return $x is UnknownType; // Error: Symbol `UnknownType` is not found } ```
Fix: Add a `use` statement to import the symbol, check for typos in the name, verify the symbol is defined in a loaded tyhpdef file, or ensure the file defining the symbol is included in the project.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP3003 (tyhp --explain); recovered from pre-generated diagnostics_reference.md

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP3004
data.value:
A symbol was declared in a scope where that type of declaration is not allowed.
Fix: Move the declaration to an appropriate scope. For example, class declarations belong at the namespace level, not inside function bodies.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP3004 (tyhp --explain); recovered from pre-generated diagnostics_reference.md

A class or interface directly or indirectly extends or implements itself, creating an inheritance cycle.
```tyhp <?tyhp class A extends B { } class B extends A { } // Error: Circular inheritance ```
Fix: Break the inheritance cycle by removing or restructuring the class hierarchy.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4055
data.value:

This is different from a duplicated member (`int|int`), which is TYHP4053.
```tyhp <?tyhp bool|false $flag; object|User $entity; ```
Fix: Remove the redundant member from the union.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP6009

File variables (`{fileName}`, `{fileStem}`, `{extension}`, `{recursiveDir}`, `{relativePath}`) are only valid in `output.publishContent` `dst`, and expand after glob matching. `{extension}`, `{fileStem}`, and `{recursiveDir}` may be empty. data.value:
An `extern` declaration must be name-only: `extern \Foo\Bar;`, `extern class \Foo\Bar;` (or `interface` / `enum`), `extern function \bcadd;`, or `extern const \FOO;` with a semicolon and no members or signature. A body, members, generics, `extends` / `implements` on the placeholder, an `as` alias, `abstract` / `final` / `readonly`, a backing type on `enum`, `extern trait`, or a parameter list / return type / value on `extern function` / `const` is an illegal declaration.
Grammar rejects most of these at parse time. This code is for visitor or binder paths that still see an invalid form.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP8029
data.value:
The kind of an `extern` placeholder does not match another declaration of the same name in the same PHP name space. `extern class Foo` against a real `interface Foo`, or `extern class Foo` against `extern interface Foo`, is a kind mismatch. A kind-unspecified `extern Foo;` is compatible with a later real class, interface, or enum. Functions, constants, and types occupy separate PHP name spaces, so `extern function Foo` may coexist with `class Foo`.
A later real declaration of the same fully-qualified name and kind silently replaces a compatible placeholder. Two externs of the same kind merge. This diagnostic is only the kind conflict. The `{1}` and `{2}` placeholders are the two kinds (for example `extern class` and `interface`).
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP8029 (tyhp --explain); blank line separates paragraphs

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP8030
data.value:
Overlay or include `partial` targeted an `extern` name. Partial would add members or attributes to a name-only placeholder, which is not allowed.
Full overlay replace with a real `class` / `interface` / `enum` / `function` / `const` of the same name upgrades the placeholder (a kind-unspecified `extern \Name;` accepts class, interface, or enum). `omit` of an extern is allowed and removes the name.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP8030 (tyhp --explain); blank line separates paragraphs

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP8031
data.value:
Overlay `partial function` names a function or method that is not in the environment left by include files and earlier overlays. The missing target is skipped; no attributes are merged.
Match the Tyhp name of an existing callable. `partial function` does not add a new symbol. Use a full overlay function or method declaration to introduce a name.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP8031 (tyhp --explain); blank line separates paragraphs

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP8032
data.value:
`partial function` is overlay-only. It merges attributes onto an existing callable without restating the signature.
Using it outside an overlay file is an error. Put name-only `partial function` declarations in an overlay tyhpdef (`extra.tyhp.package` / `tyhp.json` `"overlay"`). Include / baseline files still declare full signatures.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP8033
data.value:
A `partial function` member is only valid inside an overlay `partial` type. That is the merge path that keeps other members and unions attributes onto the matching method.
Write `partial class DateTime { #[\Tyhp\Optimize\Pure] partial function format; }`. A full overlay class replace restates methods with their signatures instead.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP8033 (tyhp --explain); blank line separates paragraphs

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP8034
data.value:
The semicolon header form `partial class Foo<T>;` (also interface / trait / enum) is overlay-only. It replaces written header clauses on an existing type and keeps unlisted members.
Using it outside an overlay file is an error. Put header-only `partial` declarations in an overlay tyhpdef (`extra.tyhp.package` / `tyhp.json` `"overlay"`). Include / baseline files still use brace `partial` to add members, or a full type declaration.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP8035
data.value:
A bare overlay `partial class Foo;` has no effect: it does not change generics, inheritance, attributes, or names. It is only useful as a keep so the same overlay file can also declare `partial class Foo as Bar;`.
Add generics, `extends` / `implements`, attributes, or `as`, or pair the bare keep with an alias in the same overlay file. Otherwise omit the declaration.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP7904
data.value:
`tyhp overlay create` copies a real declaration into a hand-written overlay so that declaration can be replaced. An `extern` type is a name-only placeholder with no members; copying it would write a hollow `class { }` that looks like a complete empty type.
Write a full overlay `class` / `interface` / `enum` of the same name to upgrade the placeholder, or `omit` it. Extra `extern` names belong in an include file that regen does not overwrite, not in an overlay created from the placeholder.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP7905
data.value:
`tyhp overlay stamp` writes `@overlay-against` once per managed PHP version. Each pass uses that version's managed runtime and stamps only declarations whose `declare(php=…)` or `#[\Tyhp\Php]` gate that runtime satisfies.
This error means the managed runtime for the named version is unavailable, so that pass is skipped. Declarations that belong only to that version are left unchanged. They are not stamped from a different PHP version. Restore the managed runtime cache (the same one `generate_tyhpdef` downloads) and run stamp again.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4008
data.value:

```tyhp <?tyhp int $count = "hello"; // Error: Cannot assign type 'string' to type 'int' ```

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4320
data.value:
A value that is not an inline `fn` was passed where `PropertyPath<callable(TSource $source): TReturn>` is expected. The compiler reads the property chain out of the arrow function at compile time, so an already-built closure carries no chain it can lower.
```tyhp <?tyhp function takes(\Tyhp\PropertyPath<callable(User $u): string> $path): void {}
takes($someClosure); ```
Pass an inline arrow function instead — `takes(fn ($u) => $u->name)`. Forwarding an existing `PropertyPath` value (for example a parameter of the same type) is also accepted.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP4320 (tyhp --explain); blank line separates paragraphs

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4321
data.value:
The inline `fn` body is not a simple property-access chain rooted at the lambda parameter. Method calls, operators, function wrappers, and roots other than the parameter cannot be represented as a property path.
```tyhp <?tyhp function takes(\Tyhp\PropertyPath<callable(User $u): string> $path): void {}
takes(fn ($u) => \strtolower($u->name)); ```
Use only `->` or `?->` property accesses starting at the parameter — `takes(fn ($u) => $u->address->city)`.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP4321 (tyhp --explain); blank line separates paragraphs

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4322
data.value:
The inline `fn` body contains an expression kind that cannot be represented in an expression tree. Assignments, `await`, `yield`, `match`, `instanceof`/`is`, nested `fn`/closures, free function calls, `throw`, and similar constructs are rejected so the emitted tree stays a faithful, inspectable data structure.
```tyhp <?tyhp function takes(\Tyhp\Expression<callable(User $u): bool> $pred): void {}
takes(fn ($u) => await $u->load()); ```
Simplify the body to supported forms: property/method access, operators, casts, ternary/`??`, array access, `new`, literals, and definitely-assigned captures.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP4322 (tyhp --explain); blank line separates paragraphs

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4323
data.value:
A value that is not an inline `fn` was passed where `Expression<callable(T $arg): R>` is expected. The compiler builds the expression tree from the arrow function at compile time, so an already-built closure carries no tree it can lower.
```tyhp <?tyhp function takes(\Tyhp\Expression<callable(User $u): bool> $pred): void {}
takes($someClosure); ```
Pass an inline arrow function instead — `takes(fn ($u) => $u->age > 18)`. Forwarding an existing `Expression` value (for example a parameter of the same type) is also accepted.
data.comment: Long-form explanation for TYHP4323 (tyhp --explain); blank line separates paragraphs

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4326
data.value: `\Traversable` is an engine interface. Only `\Iterator` and `\IteratorAggregate` may extend it. Classes, enums, interfaces, and traits list `\Iterator` or `\IteratorAggregate` instead of `\Traversable`. Listing both (for example `implements \Iterator, \Traversable`) is also rejected.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4327
data.value: `#[\Tyhp\PhpType]` replaces the emitted PHP type of a parameter, function or method return, property, or typed constant. It is not a valid target on a class, interface, trait, enum, enum case, catch type, local variable, or property hook. Put the attribute on the property or on the `set` parameter instead of on `get`/`set`.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4328
data.value: Each typed use of a `yield` expression (for example `int $x = yield` or `foo(yield)` when `foo` takes `int`) constrains generator `TSend` — the type of `Generator::send()`. Several such targets are intersected. If that intersection is empty (for example `int` vs `string`), no send value can satisfy every site. Untyped `$x = yield` does not constrain `TSend` (it stays `mixed`).

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4329
data.value: `#[\Tyhp\PhpType]` takes a PHP type-hint spelling such as `mixed`, `int`, `string|int`, or `?\Foo`. The constructor argument must be that string; invalid spelling (for example `int[]`, `?mixed`, or a missing argument) is a compile error. Checker types are unchanged; only the emitted PHP type uses the hint.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4330
data.value: PHP array offsets cannot be arrays. Tyhp structs erase to arrays, so `ArrayAccess<SomeStruct, TValue>` is not a legal homogeneous map (that spelling is `TKey` plus default `TValue`, not a per-key shape). Use `int`, `string`, `int|string`, or an object key type. Per-key struct maps are `ArrayAccessShape`.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4331
data.value: An `ArrayAccessShape` index must be a struct-key literal (or a finite union of those keys). A wide `string`, `int`, or `mixed` key is not enough; narrow the key or assert it with `as`.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4332
data.value: `ArrayAccessShape` has a closed key set from `TStruct`. Append (`$obj[] =`) is only legal on homogeneous `ArrayAccess`. Write a known key such as `$obj['host'] = …`.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4333
data.value: For each finite struct key `K`, `offsetGet` / `offsetSet` is checked with `$offset` assumed `K`. A key is covered only by a reachable value return (`offsetGet`) or a write of `$value` (`offsetSet`) of that field's type. `throw` and `never` do not cover an unhandled key; `match` is sufficient but not required.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4334
data.value: After `bindTo($x)` or `bindTo($x, 'static')` the leftover `TScope` is unchanged. `$newThis` must still be an instance of that scope class (or of `TThis` when the stored scope is gradual). An explicit object `$newScope` requires `TNewThis` to be a subtype of that object's type; a string `$newScope` must be `__SuperTypeName<TNewThis>` (an ancestor name, not a descendant). `call($newThis)` is a temporary bind: `$newThis` must be a non-null object compatible the same way. Gradual `TThis` (`object|null` / bare `\Closure`) does not prove an error.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4335
data.value: The token `'static'` on `bind` / `bindTo` means "keep the old stored `TScope`". It is not a class-name string and must not appear as a Closure type argument. Write `\Closure<callable(…): mixed, TThis, TScope>` with a real scope type, or omit `TScope` so the default `__ClosureScope<TThis>` is used.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4336
data.value: PHP refuses to rebind some closures. Arrow functions, first-class callables, and `fromCallable` of a non-Closure cannot change `$this` or scope. Binding `$newThis` or `$newScope` to an internal (engine) class is also forbidden. A gradual `\Closure` annotation does not prove the value is non-rebindable.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4337
data.value: `\UnitEnum` and `\BackedEnum` are engine interfaces. Classes, interfaces, and traits cannot implement or extend them. Enumerations are already `\UnitEnum` (and `\BackedEnum` when backed) and must not list those interfaces in `implements`. Only `\BackedEnum` may extend `\UnitEnum`.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4338
data.value: The engine supplies `cases` on every enumeration and `from` / `tryFrom` on backed enumerations. Redeclaring those methods is an error.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4339
data.value: PHP constructors are exempt from override signature checks, so `#[Override]` is invalid on `__construct` even when a parent constructor exists. This error is reported at every `output.phpVersion`. Use `#[Override]` on methods or (PHP 8.5 or later) properties that actually replace a parent or interface member. A method or property that does not override uses TYHP4129 instead.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4340
data.value: `#[\Tyhp\NativeTypeTest]` marks a free function or concrete static method as the native lowering for `$x is T`. Instance methods, abstract or interface methods, closures, and other declarations cannot be that lowering; emit is `fqn($x)` or `\Class::method($x)` with the guarded first parameter.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4341
data.value: The attribute does not take a type argument. `T` is the type-guard return of the same function: the first parameter must be named in `$param is T` (not `$other is T` and not an index subject such as `$array[$key] is T`).

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4342
data.value: `T` must be a single type after transparent alias expansion. Unions (`int|string`), intersections, and nullables (`?string`) stay on `\Tyhp\Type::is` at `$x is …` sites; mark a guard only when it tests one exact type (for example `string`, `int`, or a class name).

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4343
data.value: `$x is T` emits `fqn($x)` and does not pass further arguments. Extra parameters after the guarded first parameter must all have defaults (or be variadic) so a one-argument call is valid.

data.name: EXPLAIN_TYHP4344
data.value: Only one callable may be the native test for a given `T`, including overlapping guarded types (for example `string` and `int|float|string`). Canonical PHP builtins such as `is_int` are marked; aliases such as `is_integer` / `is_long` stay callable but do not win `$x is int`. Concrete static methods are allowed; instance and abstract methods are not.
